newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 23.

text.p: PRAVO - A proposal for a new pension law, which would enable citizens to go into early retirement, was approved by the cabinet on Wednesday. The new law changes the 0.6 percent reduction in pension allotments for every 90 days prior to reaching the legal age to a smaller reduction of 0.3 percent.

- By the end of this year, Skoda Mlada Boleslav will begin manufacturing Skoda automobiles in Russia, and yearly approximately 5,000 automobiles should be manufactured there. Skoda will be working in cooperation with Avantgard Safanovo in the Smolensk region west of Moscow.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka, the new pension law will increase the amount which the government budget gives to pension by 700 million crowns.

- Ceska Sporitelna is planning to become the first bank providing mortgage credit in progressive payments, which will create an advantage mainly for young families who due to their low incomes usually do not have the possibility to get credit.

- Expansion of the EU and NATO was the main theme of an interview between President Vaclav Havel and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl yesterday in which Kohl stated that membership does not concern only economics and finance, but also cultural identity.

- The holding company Paramo, a producer of oil products increased its sales over 1995 by 33.5 percent to 4.5 billion crowns last year. Its subsidary Paramo Trysk wants to substantially expand its network of service stations this year.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Finance Ministry announced yesterday that the largest fund from the second wave of coupon privatisation, A-Invest, is under compulsory administration. Director of A-Invest, Pavel Dvoracek, considers the decision from the ministry surprising and that it is possibly due to the ministry's wishes to supervise the wide variety of funds which A-Invest administers, one of which is the open-end fund Agrobanka, which is the largest fund of its kind in the country.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Interior Minister Jan Ruml insists that the documents which Chairman of Parliament Milos Zeman presented to him yesterday pertaining to alleged illegal observation of politicians by the secret service (BIS) and Interior Ministry mostly come from anonymous sources and in no way tie the BIS and the Interior Ministry to any illegal activities. --Prague Newsroom 42-2-24-23-0003
